top_story.headline: Vega for Congress tells the FEC that 39 fraudulent $99.99 debit card charges drained $3,899.61 from its campaign account
top_story.dek: The New York House challenger's committee filed the Form 99 on November 2, the day before Election Day, and says the charges are being disputed with its bank and reported to police.
paragraphs: Vega for Congress, the principal campaign committee of Democratic House challenger Jose David Vega (NY-15), filed a Form 99 saying its Key Bank checking account was hit by 39 unauthorized debit card transactions of $99.99 each on the night of October 22 into the early morning of October 23, 2026. Each carried the merchant description 'E-Z*Passny Payment New York Ny' and together they total $3,899.61. The committee says its one legitimate E-ZPass charge that day was $16.66.

Treasurer Adrian Spector Pearl says the card was his, had recently been replaced by the bank, never left his possession, and that Key Bank confirmed the charges used that card. According to the filing, the bank canceled the card and opened an investigation that could take up to 90 days, and the matter was reported to the NYPD's 84th Precinct Detective Squad. The committee says E-ZPass could not help trace the charges from the card number and amounts alone.

The committee says it will report the charges on its next Form 3 as fraudulent or unauthorized, show any bank credits as other receipts, and make a cash-on-hand adjustment if the loss becomes permanent. The filing treats the loss as outside theft, not misuse by the committee or its agents. A separate keyword hit on iPowerPolitics Super PAC, Inc. turned out to be the 'lost/stolen debit card' boilerplate on a bank statement showing no activity.

sections.headline: One sitting House member received an RFAI
paragraphs: Rep. Scott Franklin (R-FL) is the only sitting lawmaker with a new filing, and it is a routine donor-identification letter with a note about overdue candidate loans.

items: FEC asks Rep. Scott Franklin (R-FL) to fix incomplete employer and occupation entries for donors, and notes candidate loans overdue since 12/31/2020. The entries it calls unacceptable are 'Information Requested/Information Requested,' 'Self-Employed/Bus Owner' and 'Self-Employed/Owner.' The letter on the October Quarterly Report (07/30/2026 to 09/30/2026) says an overdue loan from the candidate's personal funds may be treated as a contribution if new terms are not disclosed. Response due 12/07/2026. Treasurer is Bradley T. Crate. (RFAI)

sections.headline: 39 more RFAIs, all dated November 2 with a December 7 response date, mostly summary-page math and missing signatures
paragraphs: The batch is dominated by template problems: Column B totals that do not add up, reports the FEC says were not signed, and independent-expenditure reports that do not match Schedule E. Items below are grouped by type. Treasurer Howie Stanger is the treasurer on letters to both Kiros for Congress and Mijente PAC, and several committees received two letters.

items: FEC asks Kiros for Congress, the committee of Colorado House challenger Melat Kiros (D), to correct Column B totals on Lines 11(a)(i) and 11(a)(ii) of its October Quarterly Report. The letter says Column B must show only election-cycle totals from 11/6/2024 through 11/3/2026. Treasurer Howie Stanger also signs for Mijente PAC. (RFAI)
FEC sends Kiros for Congress a second RFAI, on its Pre-General Report, over the same Column B totals problem. The wording matches the October Quarterly letter. (RFAI)

FEC asks Scott Singer for Congress-GTM Nominee Fund: FL-25, the committee of Florida House challenger Scott M. Singer (R), to provide its Column B totals on the October Quarterly Report. Treasurer is Lisa Lisker. (RFAI)

FEC asks Scott Singer for Congress-GTM Nominee Fund: FL-25 for Column B totals on its Pre-General Report and to explain why Line 8 on the Summary Page does not equal Line 27 on the Detailed Summary Page. The same treasurer, Lisa Lisker, received the October Quarterly letter. (RFAI)

FEC asks Ty Pinkins for Congress, the committee of Mississippi Senate challenger Ty Pinkins (I), to correct Column B totals on 18 lines of its October Quarterly Report. The lines run from 6(a) through 22, and the letter says Column B should cover only 11/4/2020 through 11/3/2026. Pinkins is listed as his own treasurer. (RFAI)

FEC asks Leadership for Enterprise and Opportunity PAC to correct Column B totals on 11 lines and its Line 8 cash-on-hand calculation. The letter on the October Quarterly Report says Column B should reflect only calendar-year-to-date totals. Treasurer is Louis Schiazza. (RFAI)

FEC asks Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association Inc. Political Action Committee (OOIDA-PAC) to correct Column B totals on nine lines of its July Monthly Report. The report covers 06/01/2026 to 06/30/2026. Treasurer is Angela Burnell. (RFAI)

FEC tells EyePAC Political Action Committee for American Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery that its Line 8 calculation on the October Quarterly Report appears incorrect. Closing cash on hand must equal the closing calendar-year-to-date cash on hand. (RFAI)

FEC asks Boston Scientific Corporation Political Action Committee (BSC PAC) to fix donor employer and occupation entries reading 'Information Requested'. Among the entries it calls unacceptable are 'Boston Scientific / Information Requested,' 'BSC / Information Requested,' 'BSCI / Information Requested' and 'Information Requested / Analyst, Prin Business Process.' Treasurer is Lauren Tengler. (RFAI)

FEC tells Halff Associates Fed PAC that its 12 Day Pre-General Report (10/01/2026 to 10/14/2026) was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on its Statement of Organization. Treasurer is R. C. Plugge, Jr. (RFAI)

FEC raises the same signature problem with National Association of Residential Property Mangers, Inc. Political Action Committee (NARPM PAC) over its amended April Quarterly Report. The amended report covers 01/01/2026 to 03/31/2026 and was received 09/25/2026. The FEC record spells 'Mangers' this way. (RFAI)
FEC raises the same signature problem with Our City PAC over its October Quarterly Report. Treasurer is Marlon Bolton of Tallahassee. (RFAI)
FEC raises the same signature problem with Reopen America Political Action Committee over its October Quarterly Report. Treasurer is Crystal Krason. (RFAI)

FEC raises the same signature problem with Transport Workers Union Voice over its October Quarterly Report. A second letter on the same committee covers its Pre-General Report. Treasurer is Matt Hettich. (RFAI)
FEC sends Transport Workers Union Voice a second signature RFAI, this one on its Pre-General Report. (RFAI)

FEC asks Forward Party Victory Fund Inc to have its treasurer sign the Schedule E on a 24-hour notification report received 10/15/2026. The treasurer's signature attests the expenditures were not coordinated with any candidate or committee. Treasurer is Mike McCauley. (RFAI)

FEC asks Health Care Saves Lives to explain possible missing or late 24-hour independent-expenditure reports, an unitemized expenditure supporting 'Bains, Jasmeet,' and payment dates for payee 'Canal Partners Media' that do not match Schedule E. The three-item letter is on its July Quarterly Report (05/14/2026 to 06/30/2026). Treasurer is Oscar Lopez, who also received the letter below. (RFAI)

FEC asks Health Care Saves Lives why an amended pre-primary report shows $169,997.68 more in vendor debts than the original. The four-item letter on the Amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (04/01/2026 to 05/13/2026, received 07/15/2026) also asks for the recipient committee's full name on an in-kind contribution. It also cites possible missing 48-hour reports and 48-hour reports naming 'Campa-Najjar, Ammar,' 'Denney, Audrey,' 'Wilpert, Marni Von' and 'McGuire, Mike' as payees that do not match Schedule E. (RFAI)

FEC asks Mijente PAC why Schedule E shows memo entries for independent expenditures on behalf of 'Gutierrez, Leticia' and 'Talarico, James' with no supporting Schedule D. The letter is on the October Quarterly Report. Treasurer Howie Stanger also signs for Kiros for Congress. (RFAI)

FEC asks South Jersey Leadership to clarify 'General Consulting Services' and to reconcile 24-hour reports naming payee 'Vision Media Marketing, Inc.' with its Schedule E. The letter is on the July Quarterly Report. Treasurer is Jean Swibinski. (RFAI)

FEC asks American Liberty Foundation for a complete amended 24-hour report with the purpose of its independent expenditures. The report was received 10/26/2026. Treasurer is Thomas Datwyler of Hudson, Wisconsin. (RFAI)
FEC asks UnidosUS Action PAC for an amended 24-hour report with the payee's complete mailing address. The report was received 10/31/2026. Treasurer is Lautaro Diaz. (RFAI)

FEC asks Deborah Adeimy for Congress, the committee of Florida House challenger Deborah Adeimy (R), about contributions that appear to exceed limits and earmarked contributions missing conduit details. The two-item letter on the October Quarterly Report reviews the $3,500, $2,000 and $5,000 per-election limits and the 60-day refund, redesignation and reattribution rules. Dollar amounts are in an attachment not in the text. Treasurer is David Satterfield. (RFAI)

FEC asks Oliver Gilbert for Congress, the committee of Florida open-seat Democratic candidate Oliver G. Gilbert III, to disclose conduit details for earmarked contributions on its Pre-General Report. Treasurer is Gloria Maggiolo, who also received the October Quarterly letter below. (RFAI)

FEC sends Oliver Gilbert for Congress a four-item RFAI on its October Quarterly Report covering excessive contributions, post-primary money, missing 48-hour notices and conduit details. One item says contributions received after the 2026 primary but designated for it can be kept only up to net debts outstanding. Another says the committee may have missed 48-hour notices for contributions of $1,000 or more after the close of books for the 12 Day Pre-Primary Report. The 8-page letter went to the same treasurer, Gloria Maggiolo. (RFAI)

FEC tells The Farm Credit Council Political Action Committee that its August Monthly Report shows an apparent excessive contribution to a federal candidate. The letter notes the refund appeared on its 12-Day Pre-General Report (10/1/26 to 10/14/26). The multicandidate limit cited is $5,000 per election. Treasurer is Jenny Mesirow. (RFAI)

FEC asks Alabama Republican Party to explain 'STRATEGY CONSULTING & EXPENSES,' payroll memo entries for 'PAYCHEX' and a transfer-in from the Republican National Committee tied to 'PRINTING EXPENSE: LANYARDS'. The three-item letter on the September Monthly Report (08/01/2026 to 08/31/2026) asks whether the lanyard spending was exempt party activity. Treasurer is Reed Phillips. (RFAI)

FEC asks Alabama Republican Party why its amended August Monthly Report shows $34,980.11 more in receipts than the original. The amended report covers 07/01/2026 to 07/31/2026 and was received 09/18/2026. The committee's treasurer, Reed Phillips, also received the letter above. (RFAI)

FEC asks Save Social Security and Medicare Now to clarify 'data rental' and to explain a voided or returned check on Schedule B. The letter is on its amended October Quarterly Report, received 10/20/2026. It asks whether the check was reissued and how the committee avoided a prohibited in-kind contribution. Treasurer is Mary Ellen Gottlieb. (RFAI)
FEC asks Midland County Republican Committee - Federal, a Michigan local party committee, why its October Quarterly Report has no Schedule H1 allocation ratio. Treasurer is Jacqueline Medema. (RFAI)

FEC asks FASPAC Fareway Stores Inc PAC to identify its connected organization or change its committee type. The amended Statement of Organization, received 10/07/2026, marks it as a separate segregated fund. The letter says such a fund's name must include its connected organization. Treasurer is Scot Kinne. (RFAI)

FEC asks North Dakota Long Term Care PAC to identify its connected organization on its Statement of Organization. It raises the same separate-segregated-fund naming rule as the FASPAC letter. Treasurer is Reier Thompson. (RFAI)

FEC asks Norwin Penn Trafford Area Democrats to identify a connected organization and to use the current Form 1. Its Statement of Organization checks the separate-segregated-fund line, and the letter says Form 1 was revised in June 2012. Treasurer is Michael Joseph Vranesevic. (RFAI)

FEC asks La Luz to explain transfers with 'BLUE DEMS PAC' that are not listed as an affiliated committee. The letter asks the Washington, D.C. committee for an amended Statement of Organization. Treasurer is Jay Petterson. (RFAI)

FEC tells Wellpath PAC its name must include the full connected organization, 'New WPCC Parent, LLC'. The letter is on its amended Statement of Organization, received 10/20/2026. Treasurer is Marc Goldstone. (RFAI)

FEC asks Grassroots Organizing for Better Election Results PAC to confirm it had 51 contributors by 8/10/26 for multicandidate status. The letter on its Form 1M says the committee does not yet appear to qualify. Treasurer is Cabell Hobbs of Austin. (RFAI)
FEC sends Top ShotPAC a similar Form 1M letter about its 51st contributor on August 25, 2026. The Baton Rouge committee's treasurer is Amanda Maloy. (RFAI)

FEC tells presidential candidate Jamill Crenshaw (R) that the election year on his Form 2 appears incorrect. The Las Vegas filer has no committee ID in the record, only a candidate ID. Response due 12/07/2026. (RFAI)

FEC tells Emmett White, a PAC, that its October Quarterly Report must be re-filed on FEC Form 3P. The report (07/01/2026 to 10/18/2026) was received 10/18/2026. The letter says a Form 99 cannot substitute for the Form 3P. White is also the treasurer. (RFAI)

sections.headline: A fraud report, a zero-activity bank statement and a 'test' filing among 16 Form 99s and related filings
paragraphs: The batch includes Vega for Congress's fraud notice, which is today's top story. Several items are FEC notices telling paper filers to file electronically, and a few are candidate paper filings whose text layer was partly unreadable.

items: Vega for Congress tells the FEC that 39 fraudulent $99.99 debit card charges totaling $3,899.61 hit its Key Bank account on October 22 and 23. The committee says the bank is investigating and the NYPD has the report. See the Top Story. (Form 99)

iPowerPolitics Super PAC, Inc. files a First Horizon Bank statement showing no activity and a $160.00 balance for July 2026. The statement shows $0.00 in deposits and withdrawals, and no cover letter explaining why it was filed is readable. The 'stolen' keyword hit is the bank's boilerplate on reporting a lost or stolen debit card. (Form 99)

Solventum Corporation Political Action Committee tells the FEC it refunded an excessive contribution from Carlos Alban on October 22, 2026. The letter, dated October 23, says the refund will appear on the post-general report due December 3, 2026. Treasurer is Jennifer Lynn Nieto Carey. (Form 99)

Tom Perriello for Congress tells the FEC it amended its filings to list Perriello Victory Fund and Virginia Congressional Victory Fund 2026 as joint fundraising representatives. The letter responds to an RFAI dated October 25 about transfers on Line 12 of its October Quarterly Report. Treasurer is Lauren Decot Lee. (Form 99)
American Resolve PAC Inc. tells the FEC it amended its July Quarterly Report on 10/14/2026 so Schedule E matches a Form 24 filed 5/4/2026. Treasurer is Staci Goede. (Form 99)

Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs, the Virginia House challenger behind Elizabeth for Virginia (D), forgives the remaining $35,956.33 of her personal loan to her campaign. It is a short paper letter addressed to FEC analyst Michael Dobi. (Filing)
Red Gold, Inc. Political Action Committee files a Form 99 whose entire text is 'Test to try new passwword.' The Elwood, Indiana committee gave no other explanation. (Form 99)

FEC tells Ahsen for Virginia, the committee of Virginia independent challenger Ahsen Mujeeb Malik, that its paper October Quarterly Report does not count and must be filed electronically. The report (01/17/2026 to 09/30/2026) was received on paper 10/15/2026. The notice warns that paper filers may be treated as nonfilers under the Administrative Fine Program. (Filing)

FEC sends presidential candidate Jonathon Mark Rice's John Rice for President the same paper-filing notice. The input shows it duplicates the Ahsen for Virginia notice apart from numbers and image IDs. (Filing)

FEC tells Espinoza for Texas, the committee of Green Party House challenger Eddie Espinoza, that its paper July Quarterly Report must be filed electronically. The report (09/13/2025 to 09/30/2026) was received on paper 10/08/2026. (Filing)

FEC tells Kentucky Party that a paper filing received 07/15/2026 will not count as its Amended 2025 Year-End Report. The amendment must be filed electronically. Treasurer is Geoffrey M. Young. (Filing)

FEC confirms that Jeremy Levan for President 2028, a presidential candidate's committee (independent), must continue filing monthly. The notice acknowledges a 10/7/2026 request to change filing frequency. The next reports are the November Monthly due 11/20/2026, December Monthly due 12/20/2026 and Year-End due 1/31/2027. (Filing)

Makiba Gaines for Congress, the Virginia House challenger committee (Independent Party), files a paper Form 3 showing $4,257.62 in receipts, $3,302.62 in disbursements and $955.00 cash on hand. The filing lists $2,086.56 from the candidate and $2,096.06 from donor Joshua Gaines of Chesapeake. Disbursements include flyers, yard signs and $1,200 to Wix.com Inc. for website maintenance. The reporting period is hard to read in the scan. (Filing)

Neelam Taneja Perry PAC files an 18-page paper Form 3 whose figures are mostly handwritten and unreadable in the PDF text. The attached Truist statements show the balance falling from $12,642.11 on 06/30/2026 to $3,562.22 on 07/31/2026, with $8,082.66 in non-check withdrawals. They include airline, fuel and restaurant debit card charges. FEC records list two candidate entries for Dr. Neelam Taneja Perry, one NPA in Florida's House race and one Republican in the Florida Senate race. (Filing)

Ms Rand for President, the committee of Republican presidential candidate Rachel Lydia Rand, files a paper Statement of Organization. She is listed as treasurer and custodian of records, and the bank is Rivermark Community Credit Union. The committee-type checkboxes could not be read from the scan. (Filing)
Ohio Coal Association PAC files a paper Statement of Organization whose handwritten entries could not be read from the PDF. The filing is stamped as received by email. (Filing)

sections.headline: Two negative entries of $10,000 or more, one explained and one not
paragraphs: Two large negative Schedule A entries were found. A large negative amount is FEC's convention for a voided, reversed or refunded transaction and is usually mundane. One carries a routine reattribution description and the other has no description.

items: Team Tafoya shows a negative $12,000 entry for donor Mark Davis, described as a reattribution to his spouse. The entry is dated 7/30/2026. (Filing)
Citizens for Boyle shows a negative $31,786.02 entry involving Vanguard dated 9/30/2026. The entry carries no description. (Filing)
